claims.text: A high-configurational-entropy multi-principal-element binder will suppress Mg or elemental volatility at 850–900 °C.
A multi-principal-element binder will suppress grain coarsening at 850–900 °C.
Mechanical alloying followed by SPS at 850–900 °C will produce a microstructure exceeding 95% theoretical density.
The proposed processing route will produce a single-phase-like microstructure with no secondary phase exceeding 5 vol%.
The resulting microstructure will improve oxidation and corrosion resistance and lower corrosion current density relative to standard-sintered samples.
The processed alloy will retain a bulk density below 6 g/cm³.
High-energy mechanical alloying followed by SPS is an appropriate route for forming the proposed alloy at 850–900 °C.
Vacuum or inert argon will mitigate Mg volatility during sintering.
Applying 30–50 MPa during SPS will facilitate densification without excessive grain growth.
High configurational entropy and lattice strain will stabilize a highly distorted, single-phase-like solid solution matrix.
The distorted solid-solution matrix will act as a kinetic barrier to elemental segregation.
Atomic-radius mismatch and high configurational entropy create lattice distortion and sluggish diffusion kinetics in the proposed Mg-Cr-Ni-Co-Fe system.
Sluggish diffusion will suppress dissolution-precipitation, secondary-phase formation, segregation, and grain coarsening.
A dense, chemically homogeneous microstructure will eliminate micro-electrical or micro-galvanic couples responsible for selective corrosion.
Standard sintering of Mg-transition-metal alloys in the 800–1000 °C regime causes incomplete densification, severe segregation, brittle secondary phases, and poor corrosion resistance.
Below 800 °C, relative density fails to exceed 90% because atomic diffusion is insufficient.
Above 1000 °C, severe Mg volatility and Mg loss cause porosity and phase instability.
The 900 °C sample should have a lower corrosion current density than the 800 °C sample.
Mg loss at 900 °C should not exceed 5 wt% relative to the 800 °C sample.
